description.narrative: Bio-resurser Innovations nätverk för Östafrika utveckling är en tvärvetenskaplig forskning och innovation finansieringsmekanism för biovetenskaper och produktorienterad innovationer i Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi och Ethiopia. BIO-INNOVATE nisch är fokus på tillämpningar av bio-resurser innovationer för att stödja hållbar tillväxt och anpassningsförmåga till klimatförändringar.

The Bio-resources Innovations Network for Eastern Africa Development is a multidisciplinary research and innovation competitive funding mechanism for biosciences and product oriented innovation activities in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and Ethiopia. The BIO-INNOVATE niche is a focus on applications of bio-resources innovations to support sustainable growth and adaptability to climate

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The overall objective of the program is to create, promote and strengthen bioscience innovation platforms involving a broad mix of disciplines and actors for sustainable and intensified utilization and integration of eastern Africa’s bio-resources into economic growth and development of the region by 2014. At the program level there are four specific objectives: Specific Objective 1: Bioscience innovation platforms for sustainable and intensified utilization and integration of the Eastern Africa’s bio-resources into economic growth and development created by 2014 Specific Objective 2: The Program and Project teams and collaborating partners have common understanding of Results-based Management and are reflected in a consistent approach in their log frame, reporting, monitoring, self-assessment and evaluation processes by 2014. Specific Objective 3: Awareness and advocacy efforts by the Program in promoting the use of bioscience innovations to harness bio-resources for sustainable utilization and integration of these innovations into eastern Africa’s economic development increased by 2014 Specific objective 4: Additional resources to increase Programmatic activities mobilized by 2014 At programmatic level, among other results , there were two major events that were successfully executed during this period, namely, the regional scientific conference and the Program mid-term evaluation. The conference attracted over 150 participant from 21 countries . A total of 35 papers and 22 posters were presented. The mid-term review outcomes and recommendations were discussed at the Technical Advisory Committee and decisions endorsed at the ILRI-Sida annual review meeting, and are currently being implemented. As a result at the project level the contract with project 8 was terminated due to non performance land there was a marked slowing down of activities in the first half of the year for the remaining projects due to adjustment of the activities with more focus on achieving results at outcome level. The teams were requested to review their work plans for the rest of the project duration and funds disbursed in accordance with the adjustments. Therefore most activities were resume in the second half of the year and had spilled over to first half of 2015 in order to accomplish earmarked activities in line with the approved work plan and Budget for project form July2014-May 2015.
In an overall assessment, 2010-2015, in total 8 technologies were developed, out of which 2 technologies have been shown to have a favourable business case and have been recommended for business plan development as a prerequisite for commercialization. With regard to capacity building, in total 38 MSc-students and 7 PhD-students were trained in the program.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
